doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Studio work, Rudy Van Gelder and Freddie Hubbard
title: Rudy Van Gelder's microphone setup
summary: Laws describes the close single Shure mic on his mouthpiece, the isolation booth, and Van Gelder's secrecy about equipment.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So you can’t tell me what kind of mics he used to capture your sound.
I can tell by the shape of them, because I know what they look like.
Do you remember specifically any brand name?
Very simple. The one he used for me was a Shure – S-h-u-r-e.
Right, I mean, okay, but do you know the model number? or describe it?
It was a Shure mic, just a boom Shure, and it put one of those – a wind screen over it. But it’s not so much that as what he did with the dials on the consol.
But you said he had it right close, close mic on the mouthpiece.
Right up there. He always wanted to mic me closely, right there on the mouthpiece.
A single mic. Not one on either end.
Single mic, and I was in a booth, always in a booth, isolated.
That gives us a little more insight, but I know Rudy safeguards his secrets.
